newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian mineral exports at record in 95/96.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian mineral exports at record in 95/96.

text.p: The value of Australia's mineral and energy exports rose 12 percent to a record A$33.9 billion in the year to June, The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Wednesday.
"The stronger performance reflected both higher world prices and increased export volumes for most minerals and energy commodities," ABARE executive director Brian Fisher said.
The fastest export rises were for uranium, which jumped by 29 percent to A$242 million from A$188 million, and alumina, up 22 percent to A$2.71 billion from A$2.23 billion.

Refined gold exports rose 20 percent to A$5.61 billion from A$4.69 billion, nickel rose 18 percent to A$1.16 billion from A$978 million, and coking coal rose 16 percent to A$4.74 billion from A$4.10 billion.

The strongest rises in the petroleum sector were for refined petroleum products, up 30 percent to A$926 million from A$714 million, liquefied petroleum gas, up 27 percent to A$196 million from A$154 million, and liquefied natural gas, up 14 percent to A$1.37 billion from A$1.20 billion.
Earnings from crude oil and other refinery feedstock fell three percent to A$1.67 billion from A$1.73 billion.
The mineral resource export price index rose 3.3 percent in 1995/96 (July-June) over the previous year.
The main increases were in the coal price component and the metallic minerals price component, Fisher said in a statement.
